title: 7 Science KCPE 2008
text:
KENYA NATIONAL EXAMINATIONS COUNCIL
 KCPE 2008
 SCIENCE
 READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS CAREFULLY
 Time:1 hour 40 minutes
 1. You have been given this question booklet and a separate answer sheet. The question booklet
 contains 50 question
 2. Do any necessary rough work in this booklet.
 3. When you have chosen your answer, mark it on the ANSWER SHEET, not in this question
 booklet.
 4. Use only an ordinary pencil.
 5. Make sure that you have written on the answer sheet:
 YOUR INDEX NUMBER
 YOUR NAME
 NAME OF YOUR SHOOL
 6. By drawing a dark line inside the correct numbered boxes mark your full Index Number(i.e
 School code number and the three-figured Candidate’s number)in the grid near the top of the
 answer sheet.
 7. Do not make any marks outside the boxes.
 8. Keep the sheet as clean as possible and do not fold it.
 9. For each of the question 1-50 four answers are given. The answers are lettered A,B,C and D. In
 each case only ONE of the four answers is correct. Choose the correct answer.
 10. On the answer sheet the correct answer is to be shown by drawing a dark line inside the box in
 which the letter have chosen is written.
 Example
 In the Question booklet.
 4. Which one of the following components of blood is involved in the clotting after injury?
 A. Plasma
 B. White blood cells
 C. Red blood cells
 D. Platelets
 The correct answer is D
 1 [A] [B] [C] [D] 14. [A] [B] [C] [D] 24. [A] [B] [C] [D] 34. [A] [B] [C] [D]
 11. Your dark line MUST be within the box.
 12. For each question ONLY ONE box is to be marked in each set of four boxes.
 This question paper consists of 7 printed pages and 1 black page.
 The Kenya National Examination Council, 2008.
 1. A card with word BRICK written on it was placed in front of a mirror. Which one of the following
 shows how the word would appear in the mirror?
 2. Absorption of water in the alimentary canal of human beings takes place in the
 A. Stomach
 B. Duodenum
 C. Small intestine
 D. Large intestine
 3. Standard five pupils observed and grouped some small animals were CORRECTLY grouped?
 A. Ant, tick, spider
 B. Beetle, moth, ant
 C. Spider, weevil, beetle
 D. Tick, moth, weevil
 4. Which one of the following groups consists of non-flowering plants only
 A. Moss, grass, pine
 B. Fern, algae, pine
 C. Moss, algae, cabbage
 D. Cabbage, grass, fern
 5. Which one of the following statements about vertebrates is TRUE?
 A. Fish and amphibians have scales
 B. Amphibians and reptiles lay their eggs on land
 C. Fish and birds have constant body temperature
 D. Reptile and birds lay eggs
 6. The diagram below shows parts of a flower
 Which one of the labeled parts is NOT CORRECTLY matched with its function
 Part function
 A. W Receives pollen grains
 B. X Produce pollen grains
 C. Y Develops into seed after fertilization
 D. Z Protect inner parts of a flower
 7. Which one of the following parts of a maize grain is CORRECT matched with its function
 8. Which one of the following is NOT an excretory organ?
 A. Skin
 B. Lung
 C. Kidney
 D. Rectum
 9. Which one of the following are the percentage of carbon dioxide and nitrogen in the air?
 A. 1% and 21%
 B. 0.03% and 78%
 C. 21% and 78%
 D. 0.03% and 1%
 10. The processes I, II, III and IV in the chart below bring about changes in the state of matter
 The processes that required increase in the temperature are
 A. III,IV
 B. II,IV
 C. I, II
 D. I, III
 11. The diagram below shows a set up that was used to investigate a certain property of air
 Which one of the following would NOT be observed if the tin can was heated gently?
 A. Bubbles in the basin
 B. Drop of ink moving towards water in the basin
 C. Water level in the basin decreasing when heating is stopped
 D. Water level in the glass tube decreasing when heating is stopped
 12. Which one of the following factors will not affect sinking and floating of materials in water? The
 A. Mass of material
 B. Type of material
 C. Shape of material
 D. Size of material
 13. In which one of the following activities is LEAST needed?
 A. Writing
 B. Riding a bicycle
 C. Walking
 D. Using a pulley
 14. Which one of the following statements about a single fixed pulley is TRUE? The effort
 A. Moves shorter distance than the load
 B. And the load move the same distance
 C. Moves twice the distance the load moves
 D. Required is half the load
 15. Standard five pupils added equal amount of water to three equal amount of soil sample J, K, and
 L in funnels as shown below
 After 10 minutes the pupils measured the amount of water that had drained through each
 simple
 Which one of the following statements is a CORRECTLY conclusion from the results obtained?
 A. J has larger particle than L
 B. K has lager particle than L
 C. K has larger particle than J and L
 D. L has larger particle than J and K
 16. Which one of the following consists of magnetic materials only
 A. Tin, aluminum, copper
 B. Iron, steel, cobalt
 C. Tin, iron, copper
 D. Aluminum, steel, cobalt
 17. When breathing in the
 A. Diaphragm flattens
 B. Lungs shrinks
 C. Diaphragm becomes dome shaped
 D. Volume of the chest decreases
 18. Which one of the following LEAST conserves soil?
 A. Mulching
 B. Planting cover crops
 C. Contour ploughing
 D. Terracing
 19. A person intends to push s drum full of oil along an inclined plane would
 A. Decrease effort applied
 B. Decrease effort distance
 C. Decrease load distance
 D. Not affect the effort applied
 20. Which one of the following information is usually given when obtaining medicine from a
 pharmacy
 A. Expiry date
 B. Disposal method of containers
 C. The dose
 D. How to store the medicine
 21. The following are the tuber crops EXCEPT:
 A. Onion
 B. Cassava
 C. Arrowroot
 D. Carrot
 22. When sand particles are put in a glass of cold water and heated at the bottom the particles are
 seen to rise and fall. This is because sand particles.
 A. Are carried by hot water which comes down on cooling
 B. Rise when heated and come down on cooling
 C. Become lighter than water heated
 D. And water rise when heated and come down on cooling
 23. Which one of the following shows the 4th and 7th planets from the sun?
 A. Venus ,Neptune
 B. Jupiter, Saturn
 C. Mars, Uranus
 D. Jupiter , Uranus
 24. Which one of the following shows correct order of energy changes that place when a bulb is
 connected to dry cell to produce light
 A. Chemical->heat->electrical->light
 B. Electrical->chemical->heat->light
 C. Chemical->electrical->heat->light
 D. Electrical->heat->chemical->light
 25. Which one of the following consists of only characteristics of insects pollinated flower
 A. Sweet scented, large number of pollen grains
 B. Brightly coloured petals, sticky pollen grains
 C. Light pollen grain, sweet scented
 D. Bright coloured petals, light pollen grains
 26. Which one of the following is NOT a source of light?
 A. Moon
 B. Firefly
 C. Star
 D. Sun
 27. The chart below represents a simple classification of pollutants
 The pollutants represents by X and Y are
 X Y
 A. Factory acid rain
 B. Herbicides oil spillage
 C. Oil spillage acid rain
 D. Herbicides factory waste
 28. The most appropriate method of separating a mixture of sand and salt after addiction of water
 A. Decanting
 B. Filtering
 C. Sieving
 D. Evaporation
 29. In which one of the following processes is Oxygen NOT used?
 A. Making plants food
 B. Burning
 C. Breathing
 D. Germination of seed
 30. Which one of the following statements about HIV and AIDS is TRUE?
 A. People living with HIV and AIDS are thin
 B. HIV and AIDS is a curse
 C. Premarital sex is only mode of transmission of HIV and AIDS
 D. People living with HIV and AIDS are advised to eat small amount of food at a time
 31. Which one of the following is NOT an essential constitute of commercial animals feeds
 A. Water
 B. Vitamins
 C. Proteins
 D. Carbohydrates
 32. Which one of the following is likely to cause an increased growth of water plants in nearby river
 The presence of a
 A. Market centre
 B. Factory
 C. Garage
 D. Tea farm
 33. A child with thin and brown hair, swollen hands, feet and face is also likely to
 A. Have knock knees
 B. Appear weak and inactive
 C. Have a face like an old person
 D. Have faster heart beat
 34. Which one of the following statements is NOT TRUE about manures? They
 A. Improve the ability of the soil to hold water
 B. Blind soil particles
 C. Release nutrients very fast on the soil
 D. Improve air circulation in the soil
 35. Which one of the following is a function of fibre in the diet?
 A. Helps in getting rid of undigested food
 B. Helps in the absorption of digested food
 C. Adds nutrients to body
 D. Helps in digested of food
 36. Draining of stagnant water can prevent the spread of
 A. Cholera and typhoid
 B. Bilharzia and malaria
 C. Typhoid and malaria
 D. Helps in digestion
 37. Which one of the following DOES NOT produce electricity
 A. Bicycle dynamos
 B. Batteries
 C. Water dams
 D. Solar panels
 38. Which one of the following descriptions of beaks would be a bird that most likely feed on
 nectar?
 A. Short and curved
 B. Long and curved
 C. Shorter and strong
 D. Long and straight
 39. Which one of the following animals belongs to the same group as a weevil?
 A. Crab
 B. Mite
 C. Spider
 D. Termite
 40. Which one of the following statements is NOT CORRECT about a wind sock?
 A. Is open at both ends
 B. Gets filled with air and rises
 C. Points to the direction from which wind blows
 D. Should be placed in the open field
 41. Which one of the following examples of levers has the position of effort between the positions
 of load and fulcrum when is used?
 A. Spade
 B. Wheelbarrow
 C. Claw hammer
 D. Crow bar
 42. The diagram below represents a set up that is used to investigate a certain property of light
 The property investigated is that light
 A. Is refracted
 B. Travels in the straight line
 C. Is dispersed
 D. Does not pass through opaque materials
 43. Which one of the following groups of sources of energy consists of only renewable sources?
 A. Firewood, kerosene, waterfall
 B. Wind, charcoal, biogas
 C. Diesel, waterfall, wind
 D. Biogas, kerosene, firewood
 44. Which one of the following is NOT a reason for lighting a house?
 A. For safety purpose
 B. To discourage pests
 C. To feel warm
 D. To read comfortable
 45. The followings are ways of maintaining tools EXCEPT:
 A. Cleaning after use
 B. Greasing
 C. Sharpening
 D. Using them regularly
 46. Which one of the following effects of drugs abuse consists of only social effects
 A. Theft and lack of concentration
 B. Drugs induced accidents and truancy
 C. Rape and withdrawal symptoms
 D. Drug addiction and loss of consciousness
 47. The presence of thick white and mountain shaped clouds are sign of
 A. Heavy rain falling soon
 B. Low temperature
 C. Fine weather
 D. Strong winds blowing
 48. A lactating mother needs foods rich in iron
 A. To protect the baby against diseases
 B. For the formation of strong bones in the baby
 C. To increase milk production
 D. To replace blood lost during birth
 49. The component of soil that improves its water holding capacity is
 A. Mineral salts
 B. Air
 C. Organic matter
 D. Living organism
 50. Which one of the following BEST describe the term environment?
 A. The surrounding of living organism
 B. Where a living organism obtains food from
 C. Where a human being lives
 D. The home of living organism
